page: Amazon Web Services c8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal server belonging to the compute-optimized instance family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating up to 4.5 GHz across 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs, configured without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core). The hardware provides direct bare-metal access without hypervisor virtualization. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA encryption acceleration.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent file systems. Network connectivity is delivered with a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps. In standardized testing, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-core compute throughput, scoring 687081.94 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 183009.76 in PassMark CPU benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is strong, achieving 1035.16 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 384.2 GB/sec in write operations. Cache-line and memory throughput support high transaction levels, demonstrated by 440.57 million Redis SET operations per second and 181.95 GB/sec static web throughput.

Cost efficiency is driven by dense core allocation, providing dedicated execution pipelines per vCPU for parallel computation without virtualization penalties. A structural tradeoff is the absence of local storage, meaning I/O-intensive workloads rely on external storage performance over the 75 Gbps network interface. Given its massive thread count and memory architecture, the server fits compute-heavy batch processing, high-throughput web serving, distributed CI/CD builds, scientific simulations, and large-scale data transformation (ETL) tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server engineered for dense, parallel computing. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it contains 192 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9R45 processor cores running up to 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding a focused 2.0 GB per core ratio. The server provides 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 687081.94 on multi-core stress-ng and 1035.16 GB/sec in large-block memory read operations. Lacking local disks, the system depends on remote network volumes. This configuration fits high-concurrency workloads such as large-scale compilation, compute-intensive ETL, batch processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
